Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire
devices using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings
are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818)
548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City
Clerk's Office. For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public
comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is discussed. If you have
any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the City Clerk
at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents
related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E.
Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.

5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS

  Councilmember Brotman hiked to the top of Mount Lukens with retired Police Chief Carl
  Povilaitis and a resident, Jon Hampkins.

  Councilmember Devine stated that today was giving Tuesday. She thanked Marian Getts for
  delivering meals to the homeless on Thanksgiving.

  Councilmember Asatryan stated that there was a long list of events that she attended. She
  mentioned the Montrose Tree Lighting Ceremony that she and her colleagues attended and
  wanted to thank the Montrose Shopping Park Association. Asatryan wanted to inform
  everyone that the HI-Am Foundation will host a Komitas Quartet, which is a classical music
  concert that will take place on December 9th at 7pm at the Presbyterian Church of Glendale.
  Tickets can be purchased at https://hiamfoundation.com/. On Thursday, December 8th 6:00-
  8:30pm, Asatryan will be serving on a panel, which is hosted by the Consulate General of
  Japan in Los Angeles in collaboration with Japan House. The panel is called “World
  Assembly for Women in LA”– women’s essential role in an inclusive society; and she invited
  the women and girls to join in and participate in this event. Asatryan asked staff to provide a
  report on hosting an annual small business week, which would provide networking,
  educational workshops, and resources for small businesses and help businesses in getting
  certification as “minority and women-owned”. She indicated that the week will be May 7-13,
  2023 and hoped to get a report from staff on what it will take to organize this. Kassakhian
  seconded.

  Councilmember Najarian invited the public to attend the Holiday Tree Lighting Event on
  December 1st at 6:00pm at Glendale City Hall Perkins Plaza. He stated that it will be rainy
  this week and advised the public to turn off their sprinklers and let the rain soak the ground
  for a week before getting back on the cycle of watering again to help the ongoing drought
  situation.

  Mayor Kassakhian invited the public to attend the Annual Montrose Christmas Parade this
  Saturday at 6pm. He thanked his colleagues for attending the tree lighting in Montrose last
  weekend, which he was not able to attend due to personal obligations. Kassakhian invited
  11 29 22
  CC

  3
   the public to stop by Glendale City Hall to see the beautiful holiday decorations that were
  installed by Chris Peplow and his team. He congratulated the US Soccer Team for defeating
  Iran in the World Cup match. He acknowledged the political protests that are currently taking
  place in Iran. Kassakhian stated that he was asked by members of the Glendale community
  and the Iranian community at large where he stood on the issue of these protests. He
  acknowledged that neither he nor the people of Glendale are strangers to the politics of Iran,
  as many residents of the City trance their familial roots to Iran, and are all too familiar with
  the repressive regimes whether it was under the Shah or the post-revolution governments.
  He spoke about the death of Mahsa Amini and the restrictive and oppressive laws impacting
  women in particular. Kassakhian stated that as a parent and a human being, he believes
  that we should all condemn acts of brutality and support those who wish to live their lives
  freely without repression, violence, and restrictions on their basic human rights. Kassakhian
  stated that he stands with the brave women of Iran who are calling for their government to
  heed their cries and change so that brutality never visits another person again, that all
  people have the basic rights and freedoms of life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness and
  that no government should use violence against its own people. He hopes and prays that
  peace and freedom will prevail. Kassakhian stated that food banks such as the ones at the
  Salvation Army, Catholic Charities, and Glendale Community College, and across the region
  are low on food and asked the public if they have anything to spare to contribute to these
  food banks and help replenish their supplies. Kassakhian asked staff to provide a report on
  the cost benefit analysis of the phases of the Verdugo Wash project. Asatryan seconded.

  City Manager Roubik Golanian stated that due to forecast of rain this week, the holiday tree
  lighting at the Perkins Plaza may be cancelled and asked the Director of Public Works
  Yazdan Emrani to provide information on where to get sand and sandbags for protection
  against flash floods. Emrani stated that sand and sand bags are ready to be picked-up at
  certain locations across the city and advised the public to bring their own shovel and help
  themselves. Golanian invited the public to attend a community open house at the Glendale
  Civic Auditorium related to the proposed Scholl Canyon and Biogas project on November
  30th from 6-8pm. There will be multiple driving tours of the Scholl Canyon Landfill on
  December 3rd starting at 3:00pm. On December 7th, starting at 4:30pm, the future of the
  landfill open space and recreation uses will be discussed at the Jewel Bridges Clubhouse.

  Fire Chief Tim Ernst invited the public to the Glenoaks Wildfire Response Preparedness
  Presentation on November 30th at the Glenoaks Elementary School from 6:00-8:00pm.
